hookLine: Fast food brands love a bold ad. Let's rank the craziest ones from Burger King and McDonald's.

items.voiceLine: McDonald's sent Ronald the clown on an actual parade, with crowds cheering like he's royalty. Dated, cheesy, and deeply unsettling in hindsight. C-Tier, please retire the clown.

But Burger King's 'Moldy Whopper' ad shows their burger rotting on camera to prove there's no artificial preservatives. Bold, disgusting, and somehow it actually worked. S-Tier, they turned mold into marketing genius.
Wendy's 1984 'Where's the Beef' ad had grandmas roasting a competitor's tiny patty on a giant bun. Iconic slogan, painfully dated production. B-Tier, the line outlived the commercial by decades.

And when KFC ran out of chicken across the UK, they rearranged their own logo to spell F C K on the bucket and apologized. Reached over 200 million people. A-Tier, turning a total disaster into their best ad ever.
